Privacy Policy

Effective and last updated: October 17, 2026

Learning records stay on your device. Firebase usage analytics is optional, off by default and limited to consenting adults using a personal device for their own learning.

1. Who we are and what this policy covers

Vizancia Incorporated operates Vizancia. This policy explains personal information handling in our iPhone and iPad app, our learning and support website at odin686.github.io/VizanciaiOS/, and communications you choose to send us. Contact info@vizancia.ca for privacy questions or requests.

The app requires no account. Its lessons, games, authored simulations and learning records work locally. Versions that include Firebase do not enable usage analytics merely because the SDK is installed.

2. Privacy at a glance

You can use the learning features without agreeing to analytics.

  • No accounts, advertising, public learner profiles or live AI service calls
  • Names, answers, learning results and written reflections are excluded from automatic analytics
  • Analytics requires separate adult personal-use consent and an eligible app context
  • Local learner profiles separate work but are not password protected
  • Reports leave the app only when a person explicitly chooses a sharing destination

3. Information stored locally

The app uses Apple's SwiftData and local preferences to provide learning, remember settings and keep profiles separate. Local records can include:

  • An optional nickname, a local profile identifier, grade band and learning preferences
  • Lesson completion, practice results, review cards, XP, streaks, game records, achievements and avatar or Campus progress
  • Class Period results and activities you explicitly mark explored
  • AI Passport decisions, reasons, evidence, reflection text and dated follow-ups
  • Optional difficulty or clarity feedback, notification preferences and analytics choices

These records are not uploaded to Firebase or a Vizancia learning database. Activity exploration saves an identifier, not the answers or workshop test traces. Local profile identifiers used for switching learners and remembering analytics withdrawal are not sent as analytics user IDs.

4. Shared devices and temporary Classroom Mode

Anyone who can use an unlocked device may be able to switch local learner profiles and read their records. Use nicknames and avoid entering student names, contact details, health information or other sensitive material.

  • Temporary Classroom Mode keeps session work in a separate in-memory store
  • That session clears on ending, timeout, backgrounding or app restart
  • Personal profiles remain separate and are not erased by ending a temporary session
  • Saved personal Class Period results are different from temporary Classroom Mode
  • Project notes persist only when you explicitly save a supported reflection; ordinary workshop answers and traces stay in the session

The adult check asks someone helping to follow a reading instruction. It is an accidental-action deterrent, not a password, identity check or age-verification system.

5. When optional Firebase analytics can run

We use Google Analytics for Firebase to understand basic app usage and improve navigation and reliability. It is off by default for every learner. Settings requires a separate confirmation that you are 18 or older and use the device only for your own learning, not for children, students or other learners.

  • Onboarding must be complete
  • The selected grade band must be high school or the corresponding adult level
  • There must be exactly one local learner profile
  • Classroom Mode must be off
  • An adult must explicitly confirm personal use and allow analytics

A grade-band choice does not establish age or grant consent. Younger bands, multiple profiles and Classroom Mode exclude collection. The app does not configure Firebase on a cold launch without eligible saved consent.

6. Information Google receives after opt-in

When eligible analytics is enabled, the SDK sends usage and technical information to Google. This may include:

  • A generated app-instance identifier that groups activity from that app installation
  • Basic lifecycle and engagement events, such as first launch, sessions and engagement duration
  • Screen-view events for the fixed tab names Play, Learn, Train, Campus and Progress
  • App identifier and version, device model, operating system, language and related device or app metadata
  • Event times and approximate location derived from network information

An app-instance identifier is pseudonymous, not a guarantee of anonymity. Network requests expose an IP address to Google for delivery and processing. Google states that Analytics does not log or store individual IP addresses. Analytics does not use the device's GPS or Apple's Location Services.

  • Google's app data disclosures
  • Google Analytics data safeguards

7. Information excluded from analytics

Our analytics interface accepts fixed navigation labels, not free text or learning records.

  • No nickname, email address, local profile ID or grade band
  • No lesson answers, scores, XP, game results, review cards or learning histories
  • No AI Passport text, project notes, written responses or workshop code and test traces
  • No lesson-feedback ratings, contact lists, photos, microphone recordings or precise location
  • No account user ID, advertising identifier or vendor identifier

The app denies advertising storage, advertising user-data and advertising-personalization consent. Advertising-ID support, vendor-ID collection and automatic screen reporting are disabled. The current release does not use Firebase Authentication, Firestore, Crashlytics, Performance Monitoring, Cloud Messaging or Firebase AI services.

8. Your analytics choices and withdrawal

You may leave analytics off or withdraw consent in Settings. Withdrawing stops collection and resets local analytics data and identifiers. The app records a local withdrawal marker before attempting to save the profile preference, so a failed preference save does not restore collection on this device.

  • Switching profiles, adding a second learner, choosing a younger band or entering Classroom Mode stops collection and resets local analytics data
  • Those exclusions suspend a saved choice; the same learner's choice may resume when the app becomes eligible again
  • Settings offers withdrawal of a saved choice when it is suspended; leave a temporary class session to manage personal settings if needed
  • Reset All Progress keeps preferences, including the analytics choice, and does not withdraw consent
  • Only a newly confirmed and successfully saved opt-in clears a withdrawal marker

Withdrawal applies to future collection. It does not automatically delete information already received by Google. Reinstalling, clearing app data or resetting a local identifier is also not a request to delete previously sent information. Contact us about that information as explained below.

9. Retention and deletion

Local learning records stay until you delete the relevant records or profile, reset progress, or remove the app. Some identity and preference settings survive Reset All Progress. Backups, exported files and recovery copies have separate lifetimes.

  • As reviewed on October 17, 2026, the app's Google Analytics property retains event-level data for 2 months and user-level data for 14 months
  • Reset on new user activity is enabled, so new activity can extend the user identifier's 14-month retention window
  • These settings do not impose the same expiry on standard aggregated reports
  • Google's deletion processing and operational retention follow its applicable service terms; deletion is not instantaneous
  • Support correspondence is kept as needed to handle the request and related legal or administrative obligations; you may ask us to delete it

We review retention settings when changing analytics practices. A request to delete local progress does not delete analytics already sent, and an analytics deletion request does not erase records held only on your device.

  • Google Analytics retention controls

10. Google and international processing

Google provides the Firebase and Analytics infrastructure. Authorized people working on Vizancia can access the resulting analytics reports. Google processes information under its service terms, data-processing terms and privacy documentation, including processing needed to operate and protect its services.

Google may process analytics information in the United States and other countries where it or its service providers operate. Those countries may have different privacy laws, and their lawful-access requirements may apply.

  • Privacy and security in Firebase
  • Google's privacy policy

11. Children, families and schools

The learning app supports younger audiences with adult guidance. Optional analytics is not offered for children's or students' learning and must not be enabled on a device used for them. Adults should use temporary Classroom Mode for shared sessions and review local profiles before handing a device to another person.

A school or educator must follow its own device, privacy, sharing and approval rules. Using the app or its adult check does not establish school approval or verified parental consent. If you believe a child's information was sent to us, contact info@vizancia.ca without including the child's work or unnecessary identifying details.

12. Reports and information you choose to share

An adult may review a report and use Apple's share sheet to select a destination. Learning Reports and Class Period summaries can include a nickname, grade or module and practice results. Beta feedback reports contain structured lesson results and ratings; those details may identify a learner in context.

AI Passport text and other written responses are excluded from those reports and analytics. Review the full report before sharing and follow school rules. We receive a report only if you choose to send it to us. Copies you share, screenshots and text you copy are controlled by you and the recipients.

13. Backups, recovery copies and device removal

Apple or computer backups may contain local app data depending on device settings. If a database cannot open, the app may preserve a recovery copy on the device before starting a fresh store. Removing the app does not erase external backups, recovery copies outside its container or files already shared.

Vizancia does not operate a cloud learning-sync service and cannot remotely retrieve or erase learning records held only on your device. Device owners and school administrators manage backups and shared copies through their own systems.

14. Browser learning and website hosting

The public GitHub Pages learning player stores progress and exploration markers in that browser's local storage. Anyone using the same browser profile may see them. Its Teacher and Class Period tools save browser progress; they do not provide the native app's temporary Classroom Mode or separate learner profiles.

Use the player's reset controls or clear this site's browser data to remove local browser records. The projection page accepts no student input. Hosted page requests reach GitHub Pages, which may process IP addresses and technical access information under its own policy. This website's source adds no analytics, advertising pixels or tracking cookies.

  • GitHub's privacy statement

15. Support, Apple services and external links

If you email us, we receive your address, message, attachments and information you voluntarily include, such as an app version or device model. We use it to answer your request and manage support or privacy matters. Do not send passwords, student names, contact lists or sensitive reflection text.

App Store services, Apple-managed diagnostics or backups, email providers and destinations you open have their own privacy practices. External links and sharing use the app's adult check where required. Optional reminders are scheduled locally; Vizancia does not use a remote push-notification service.

  • Apple's privacy policy

16. Purposes, consent and disclosures

Local information supports the features and settings you choose. We rely on your separate consent for optional adult analytics; declining or withdrawing it does not prevent learning. We process support messages to respond to you and may retain information where applicable law requires it.

We do not sell personal information, show ads in the app or use learner work to train an AI service. Information may be handled by the service providers described here or disclosed when legally required, to address security or protect legal rights. Such disclosure is limited to information actually available to us.

17. Security and your device

We limit what the app permits in telemetry and keep learning records local. Firebase uses HTTPS for transmission. Local security also depends on your device passcode, operating-system protections, backups and who can use the device.

No storage or transmission method can be guaranteed completely secure. Separate learner profiles are not access-controlled accounts. Avoid sensitive information, keep devices updated and use temporary Classroom Mode for shared learning.

18. Privacy requests and complaints

Depending on applicable law and your location, you may have rights to access or correct personal information, request deletion or restrictions, withdraw consent, and raise a complaint. Email info@vizancia.ca with the subject Privacy request and describe the request without sending sensitive learning content.

We may ask for information reasonably needed to verify and handle your request. Because the app has no account and does not send local profile IDs, we may be unable to associate particular analytics records with you. We will explain technical or legal limits and respond as required by applicable law. You can also contact your local privacy regulator, including the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada.

  • Canadian privacy rights and concerns

19. Changes and contact

We update this policy when our practices change and show the revised date here. If a change requires new consent, we will request it before enabling the changed optional collection. The latest public policy is available from the app and the support website.

Privacy contact: Vizancia Incorporated, info@vizancia.ca.
